The folio gives the report of the shofar blasts at Yavneh, including the cause of the din.

The ruling on the public domain in the Land of Israel is explicitly attributed to Yoḥanan through bar Yosef.

The page gives multiple adjacent statements attributed to Yoḥanan through Yitzḥak son of R. Yosef.
The text names Yitzḥak son of R. Yose in its report from Yoḥanan.
The digital Gemara also gives the form son of R. Yose. The two Tosafot comments give differing forms.
The bar Yosef transmission in Yannai’s name is explicit.
The same name transmits Yannai about impurity by contact.
The market anecdote names Yirmeyah, bar Yosef, and the separate ruling of Yehudah son of Shimon.
The Gemara gives bar Yosef and Ravin entering Pappi’s house. Abaye comments afterward.
Bar Yosef is explicitly named reporting the arrangement of the mezuzot.
The encounter and chain of reporting are explicit. The account supplies the joint appearance of Ammi and Assi.
Tosafot introduces the identification as an interpretation given by some and notes an exception elsewhere.
The same folio’s Rashba comment discusses the decree concerning the Samaritans and competing explanations for its acceptance.
The checked primary locus gives Yitzḥak as the speaker and says Aḥa’s report in the name of Yehoshua ben Levi was inferred rather than explicit.
The local Rav Huna entry cites their joint audience with Yirmeyah. The primary passage names both interlocutors.
The primary debt episode explicitly names the judge as Ḥanina bar Pappi. The earlier citation to 170a names Nappaḥa in a parallel episode involving the same litigants.
The narrative specifies Lod and the encounter with Yehudah. The Zohar gives Yitzḥak son of R. Yose, which is why the report should not silently be assigned the heading’s patronymic.
Nappaḥa’s earlier notice explicitly lists bar Yosef, and the matched Bava Batra passage supplies their shared context.
The first gloss uses Yosef and the second Yose. The correction is Heilprin’s; these three digital occurrences remain distinct.

The Dimi entry repeats the same conjecture, giving the intended pointer. The possible kinship remains a conjecture.
